rules.recovers: nearby calls misread as far jumps, which would glue a neighbouring function into the caller
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits bl as a jump only when the target is beyond the range of `b`; the shortest far jump in five ROMs is 1,960 bytes
rules.summary: a bl closer than farJump.minDistance to its target (the far-jump idiom fails) is a call

rules.recovers: functions proposed inside another function's unreached branch arms or alignment padding
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run, so the few bytes inside it the walk never reached are still its own; a table of entry stubs `movs rX, #k; b T` that share one tail gives each entry its own constant, so an unreached copy of the entry stub is another entry, not dead code
rules.summary: a dense function's free bytes inside its extent are claimed as dead code, except unreached copies of its own `movs rX, #k; b T` entry stub

rules.recovers: heap, OAM and map routines in ARM that no accepted code refers to
rules.restsOn: hand-written ARM keeps literal pools before its code and dispatches through branch tables, and is entered through RAM copies or computed jumps
rules.summary: an ARM function at the cursor or up to armFrontPoolWords words ahead of its own pools and tables, unreached by any reference

rules.recovers: the interrupt entry and the ARM helpers the startup code installs
rules.restsOn: hand-written ARM startup code stores handler addresses computed with adr (the interrupt vector); an adr into the function's own extent is a local label, and one onto words that are claimed or do not decode names data
rules.summary: word-aligned ROM addresses past its extent that an ARM function names with adr, unclaimed and read as ARM code, are ARM functions

rules.recovers: the call graph below every accepted function
rules.restsOn: a bl (or a bx after mov lr, pc) that settles as a call enters a function
rules.summary: the targets of the calls of an accepted function are functions

rules.recovers: data and text decoded as code
rules.restsOn: every path of a compiled function decodes until it returns or jumps away
rules.summary: the walk from the entry decodes at least one instruction and hits no decode error

rules.recovers: the code after an indirect call, which an exit at the bx would leave unreached
rules.restsOn: ARMv4T has no blx; hand-written ARM and interworking code call through a register with `mov lr, pc; bx rN`
rules.summary: ARM `mov lr, pc` then `bx rN` is a call through a register: the path goes on after the bx
